name: os-windows-legacy
comment: Windows NT 4.0 through Windows 8.1 and Windows Server 2003 through 2012 R2, and the KBs no input records a product for: os/server-2008, os/server-2012, os/windows-7 and os/windows-8-1, and with them the os/windows and os/windows-server notice lines, which render no listing and collect the pre-Windows-10 one-offs. Windows is the one family split further, by OS line, because a line is a series boundary under os/ and the family is too large for one shard. Grouped by product family, not by product version as msuc-targets.json is: a seed pulls its whole series listing, shards do not share what a run has already stored, so a series two shards can both reach is fetched twice -- and family is the coarsest key that keeps a series whole.

name: dotnet-framework
comment: the .NET Framework monthly line, in 22 series, one per host OS build: dotnetframework/windows-10/1607 through 22h2, dotnetframework/windows-11/21h2 through 26h1, dotnetframework/microsoft-server/2022, /23h2 and /hci, and the bare dotnetframework line. The servicing path spells the product unhyphenated; the group name follows msuc-targets.json. They stay in one shard because splitting a family cannot make a series smaller -- it can only make one reachable from two shards. KB5019758, an Exchange Server update, is seeded here because its article is served from this product. Grouped by product family, not by product version as msuc-targets.json is: a seed pulls its whole series listing, shards do not share what a run has already stored, so a series two shards can both reach is fetched twice -- and family is the coarsest key that keeps a series whole.

name: office
comment: Office and SharePoint: office, office/hotfix and office/update/2026. Microsoft serves the SharePoint articles from the office product, so they are seeded here rather than in a shard of their own -- the family a KB is seeded under is the one its article is served from -- which is also why the Exchange Server updates KB5094140, KB5094142 and KB5094144 are here. Grouped by product family, not by product version as msuc-targets.json is: a seed pulls its whole series listing, shards do not share what a run has already stored, so a series two shards can both reach is fetched twice -- and family is the coarsest key that keeps a series whole.

name: exchange
comment: Exchange Server, in 10 series: exchange/server and its hotfix, troubleshooting and update lines, and exchange/update. The Update Catalog does not carry Exchange at all, so the article is the only record of its update and every KB is named rather than reached from a seed. Enumerated from the Exchange Server build numbers and release dates table on learn.microsoft.com, which links every SU and HU row to support.microsoft.com/help/<KB>, rather than from the msuc corpus, which carries neither the hotfix waves nor the older security updates. Grouped by product family like the rest of this file, though the reason the other groups have does not apply here: nothing expands, so no shard can duplicate another's work and the split is free. Family keeps it consistent with the groups where it is not.

name: dynamics-business-central
comment: Dynamics 365 Business Central on-premises: dynamics/business-central/update, one series of 293 seeds. Enumerated from the release-wave index pages on learn.microsoft.com, update-versions-13 through -28, which link every update row to support.microsoft.com/help/<KB>. The line renders no listing -- neither an article nor the index page serves a learnRenderLeftNav item -- so every KB is named. Seeded because the advisories do reach this family: isKBCriterionApp in vuls2 allows Dynamics, and the extracted CVRF carries 127 Dynamics and NAV KB criterions -- 13 of them with a supersedes edge whose 12 targets were, before this, all unseeded. Grouped by product family like the rest of this file, though the reason the other groups have does not apply here: nothing expands, so no shard can duplicate another's work and the split is free. Family keeps it consistent with the groups where it is not.
